After reading both changed files in full, this is a purely UI refactor: **stylist-view.tsx**: An implicit `` wrapping the flat-lay image was replaced with a `
`, and an explicit named `` button "See the full look" was added below, pointing to the same URL (`/outfits/${look.id}`). No new destination, no new data source, no new sink. **outfit-detail.tsx**: Each piece row `
` became a ``. The `p.id` value comes from the `pieces` prop which is server-supplied from the closet/outfits data model — same source that already interpolated `p.imageUrl` into `` above (an existing, higher-risk sink than an href). Sinks touched: only `next/link` `href` with relative same-origin paths (`/outfits/...`, `/closet/...`). No shell/SQL/eval/HTML/serialization/log sinks introduced. No auth check surface, no new server action, no state-changing operation. The IDs are structural URL segments; because both paths are same-origin relative, there is no open-redirect surface even if an ID contained an unusual character. No entry-point changes, no data-flow changes, no parser/validator changes, and none of the Phase 2c high-miss patterns apply (no observability sinks, no IaC, no CI trust, no allowlist edits, no permission grants, no identity teardown, no validator deletion, no state fallback, no registry fanout, no gate/action mismatch, no resource-cap change, no under-validated shell/path/loader arg).
